happened: The story opens inside a dream. The Endministrator drifts through fragments of memory: a crumbling ark silently steering away from a ravaged land, and a voice reciting a list of names. Kal'tsit, Theresa and Theresis come first, then Scout, Ace, Outcast and Whitesmith, then Buldrokkas'tee, Yelena, Kristen Wright and Rankin. The Endmin cannot place any of them, yet each name brings a quiet ache to the chest. Before the list can go on, the voice melts away like snow, leaving only frigid air and solid ground underfoot.

In the same dream the Endmin passes two tombstones. On the first, words in many languages flow over one another and seem to fight, and the Endmin understands that it records the history of countless people who now rest in that place, all telling the same tale. The second stone is split down the middle, its words barely legible, with a shadow moving in the crack. The Endmin suddenly feels that this fate could have been theirs all along, one meant for them alone, and presses forward.

The Endmin wakes aboard the OMV Dijiang, the Originium-powered Multi-surface Vessel that serves as the base and home of Endfield Industries. A young woman named Perlica, the company's Supervisor, explains that the Endmin has slept for ten years and wears a mask that suppresses and stabilises their vitals. The Endmin remembers nothing, not even Perlica, though her face seems familiar. She tells them they have always been Endfield's leader. On a tour of the ship she explains that Talos-II, usually called a planet, is really the second moon of a planet named Talos, and that much about it is still a mystery.

Perlica returns the Endmin's Protorig, a piece of Originium they once carried everywhere; every Specialist Tech Division operator has one to help triangulate tele-protocols, and this one seems to answer the Endmin's call. She recounts that the settlers planted Originium on this new world, then lost their first landing to a war they won at a terrible cost. To rebuild, the Endmin led Endfield in creating the Protorig and the Protocol Automation-Core, to be deployed across the Civilization Band for a mission called Reboot of Life, part of a Zeroth Directive issued by the Endmin. Then Comms Officer Fiona raises a maximum alert: all of Valley IV is in danger, and the landing begins.
lore: The names in the opening dream belong to the original Arknights. Kal'tsit leads Rhodes Island, Theresa and Theresis are the Sarkaz siblings at the centre of Kazdel's civil war, Scout and Ace are operators who died in the original story, and Kristen Wright is the director of Rhine Lab. That the Endmin feels grief at hearing them ties the protagonist to Terra's past. This may suggest that the Endministrator is, or is closely bound to, the Doctor of the original game, who also woke with no memory. Possibly the crumbling ark leaving a ravaged land is Rhodes Island's landship, though the text does not say so.

Perlica's account frames Endfield's people as colonists. Originium came from their distant origins and was planted on Talos-II on purpose, as a spark to make a new home, so the civilization here was carried from elsewhere rather than born on this moon. The first landing was destroyed by war against enemies that once threatened the whole civilization, and those enemies are named as a present danger again. The Protorig and the Automation-Core are the tools of the recovery, built on the same Originium that powers machines and Arts in the original Arknights.

The awakening mirrors the start of the original game, where the Doctor is freed from a sarcophagus with amnesia and told they are vital to the people around them. Here the Endmin learns that they commissioned their own awakening through the Zeroth Directive, which implies they planned for this sleep and this return. The tombstone of clashing languages, recording many lives that end in the same tale, and the split stone that feels like the Endmin's own fate are left unexplained. Possibly they stand for the people who did not survive the journey or the first war.

happened: The landing goes wrong, and the Endmin and Perlica walk to Valley IV's Hub Base through swarms of Aggeloi. Director Qin Jiangchi explains that an Ankhor crashed into the Base and keeps spawning Aggeloi; Ankhors fall from the sky and turn soil minerals, or even living matter, into new Aggeloi, and no one knows where they come from. The pair descend into the Old Factory basement, meet Miguel, who is tending the wounded with Buckflower Powder, and destroy the Ankhor's core. Operator Chen Qianyu arrives and rescues the engineer Andre, who had stayed to guard a prototype left to him by his friend Yvonne. Andre is overjoyed to see the Endmin and says they finally cracked the project the Endmin left behind, and that colleagues named Puccini and Popov died regretting they could not deliver it, before realising the Endmin remembers nothing.

Landbreaker raiders have slipped past the Aggeloi into the Hub and taken the area reserved for the Automation-Core. Perlica, Chen and the Endmin form the Endfield Crisis Team, with Perlica as acting lead; she would rather the Endmin rested, but they insist on coming. Andre adds that Ankhors come from the north and that a strike this large has not been seen in a long time. The team frees UWST crew mates, one of whom says the raiders sound northern, and notices that the Landbreakers are occupying sites rather than looting them. Only the Endmin can authorise the Protocol Automation-Core, so the Endmin deploys it and runs relay towers to the Protocol Resonance Tower, restoring power to the Base. A Landbreaker chief reports that Endfield has arrived, just as his boss predicted.

Next the team helps the damaged Originium Byproduct Processing Center. Andre admits he left parts and documents for his prototype there: upgrade parts for a large-area Arts unit he paid for himself without Director Qin's approval. Crew mates Vannikov and Dahlia had saved them, and the Landbreakers were clearly hunting these exact items on their leader's orders. Perlica wonders how raiders could know about a private order, and mentions that the UWST has spent years studying Valley IV's Æther Rift from an Æther Test Site on the Power Plateau. With help from Maymay's explosives and the arsenal engineer Semyon, Andre reboots the TA-TA Prototype, an Ætherside device. Its decrypted logs show energy pulses at the Valley Fort before the Ankhorfall, spaced almost exactly like the Ankhors' arrivals.

The Control Tower's comms node is broken, and Perlica reluctantly lets the Endmin use their old gift for sensing and fixing Originium machinery through Arts. Once contact is restored, it is clear the Valley Fort has fallen and that Landbreakers struck several key sites at once, a level of coordination Perlica thinks they do not have. Director Qin gives the team gear and a warning not to push too far. On the road west, a Landbreaker chief executes one of his own men because his boss wants disciplined warriors. The team meets Catello Wulfgard Luppino, a Specialist Tech Division operator and Landbreaker specialist, who briefly aims his gun at the Endmin. The Bonekrushers have cut power to the bridge controls, so the team restores it with the Automation-Core.

Past the bridge, a giant denstack, a Bonekrusher furnace and mark of territory, pours out a haze of airborne Blight that harms people and Originium devices. Perlica explains that the Blight comes from the Æther the way lava comes from a volcano. A captured chief names Nefarith, whom Wulfgard calls a madwoman who has broken every Landbreaker Code yet united the warring Bonekrushers. A frightened youth, Karja, leads them to a cave shelter run by the old nomad Soth, where his sister Ginny has severe Oripathy after nearly two weeks without medicine. Perlica's suppressants ease her pain, and the official summary calls them Rhodes Island medication. The team then clears a Landbreaker camp, raises an outpost with a Sub-PAC and gun towers, beats back a counterattack, and makes Soth its liaison. Soth's man Daniel opens a ventilation shaft toward the Landbreaker camp.

Before leaving, Ginny gives Perlica a drawing and asks about Uncle Mark, a UWST crew mate who carried her to safety and never returned. In the tunnels the team finds stockpiled Blighted waste and a Landbreaker trying to absorb the Blight. Wulfgard explains that the Bonekrushers worship the Æther, which they call the Deep, and shun Originium, but have never gone this far. While the team destroys the small denstacks feeding the great one, Nefarith's voice says that the land abandoned them. They free Shawna, a UWST construction crew leader, who says she saw Mark follow the Landbreakers into the Valley Fort and calls him a coward. Inside the Fort, the process ends on a dead UWST crew mate covered in wounds, still clutching an Oripathy suppressant. Possibly this is Mark, though the text does not name him.
lore: Originium and Oripathy have come with humanity from Terra. Chen recalls her history teacher saying that Oripathy patients were once shunned in many places on Terra, which matches the original Arknights, where the Infected face harsh discrimination. On Talos-II, Perlica says, infection no longer brings stigma and suppressants are effective and cheap, though there is still no cure and the disease remains common. The official summary names Perlica's medicine as Rhodes Island medication, so the pharmaceutical company of the original game, which focused on treating Oripathy, survives at least in name. Director Qin also admits that Originium mining once caused environmental and social problems, yet the settlers describe themselves as a civilization standing on Originium's shoulders.

Talos-II has its own threats that the colonists still do not understand. Ankhors fall from the north and build Aggeloi from stone or flesh, and the Æther gives rise to the Blight, which ruins people and Originium machines alike. Andre's finding that the Valley Fort's energy pulses line up with the Ankhors' arrivals, together with Landbreakers who knew about secret parts and struck several sites at once, points to someone directing this attack. This may suggest that the Ankhorfall itself was triggered or guided, a question the official summaries of later processes take up.

The process introduces the factions of the frontier. The UWST, whose crews the locals call woosters, works closely with Endfield and runs the Valley's industry. Landbreakers are raider clans bound by Codes, and the Bonekrushers among them worship the Æther as the Deep, avoid Originium and use what Wulfgard calls witchcraft such as denstacks. The Pack, to which Wulfgard belongs, works with Endfield and is despised by other Landbreakers for it. Nefarith breaks the pattern: she unites feuding clans, projects her voice through Arts, and has her followers absorb Blight. Possibly her line that the land abandoned them points to a grievance of people left outside the Civilization Band.

The Endmin's own role grows stranger. Only they can unlock the Automation-Core, they once fine-tuned Originium circuits by feel, and Andre speaks of reverse internalization technology and of printing facilities from Originium's properties. Possibly this special bond with Originium echoes the original Arknights, where the Doctor's past is tied to the mineral's origins, but the text draws no such link. Familiar Terran peoples also appear: a crew mate mentions an Elafia and a Forte, races from the original game, which shows that Terra's peoples settled here together.

happened: After the Valley Fort, Perlica reports that Nefarith, chief of the Bonekrushers, was there and blew up the bridge to the Power Plateau as she left, with the team arriving just too late; Wulfgard is pursuing her. Director Qin explains that air support is hard because Ankhors interfere with flying vehicles, and the only other route, through the Originium Science Park, is blocked by a landslide the Ankhorfall caused. Perlica is shaken by what she saw at the Fort. She asks Qin whether anyone in Valley IV has ever been able to wield the Æther directly. Qin says it is impossible, since the Æther kills anyone who touches it, the side opposing the origins of life. Perlica answers that, as the textbook footnote says, the Terrans never fully understood this planet's secrets.

The team prepares to clear the landslide. Andre's multi-purpose drill burns Originium Ore as fuel, so the Endmin researches better mining in the AIC Factory Plan, and the technician Pocus explains the Protocol Dataloggers. Crew captain Vannikov's UWST team cannot carry the Æther counters Andre insists on, so Endfield produces new protective suits for them, then uses Fitting Units to make custom parts for the construction vehicle. Perlica notes that this is the first time the AIC has built a large machine on the spot, and she imagines how many lives such capacity could improve. Qin asks for the new budget and mentions distress calls from the damaged Quarry. Perlica seems about to say something, then stops.

The mission Work Preparation is a recap in which Perlica sums up the whole Valley IV campaign, including events the later processes show. Nefarith tore open the Æther rift, and the team escorted Tata to the Æther Test Site to seal it, by way of the Science Park, where Tata's designer Yvonne repaired it. Rossi of the Pack joined them at the Origin Lodespring, and they defeated the Triaggelos in the Cradle of the Ages. Professor Crowe triggered the Utjug Order, calling down the United Syndicates' fury. Nefarith summoned the Marble Aggelomoirai; after it fell, she struck, and the Endmin tried a self-destructive Arts burst that the suppressor stopped. Tata sacrificed itself to neutralise the rift. Now Nefarith has been sighted at Wuling, aiming at the Very Large Rift.

Back in the main thread, Xaihi of the Cabal of Tranquility, who is overseeing repairs to the Dijiang, calls the Endmin up to the ship through a surface-to-orbit tele-protocol. She shows them the Manufacturing Cabin, the Reception Room, where the SOW's intelligence becomes clues to trade for credits, and a Display Section, where she praises a Cabal piece, the Sanctilamina Cathedralis Tranquillae, which has an Aggelos embedded in it. She also mentions maintaining the Stasis Core, and the Endmin jokes about not wanting another stasis nap. When a Sarkaz from the General Technological Committee calls Xaihi away, Perlica explains that the Endmin once shared critical data with the Cabal, and that Endfield's trust and tech sharing have long held the Civilization Band's factions together.

The Dijiang's Control Nexus has waited ten years for the Endmin, who built the ship, and it answers them as they restore its control authority. Perlica is moved: over the years the one in the Sarcophagus had faded from memory and become a legend, and she feared forgetting who the Endmin really was. The Zeroth Directive now requires her to share the essentials, so on the bridge, where the Endmin once liked to look down at Talos-II, she explains the Æther and the dangers they face. Nefarith, she warns, is a sign of what is coming; no one like her has appeared for many years, and history may repeat itself. She wishes she had never let the Endmin leave the ship, but the Endmin reassures her, says it feels good to be back, and the team rests before returning to Valley IV.
lore: The Æther is presented as the great unknown of Talos-II. It is lethal to the touch, it gives rise to the Blight, and Endfield's people learned to call it the side opposing the origins of life, a phrase they attribute to the Terrans while admitting the Terrans did not fully understand this world. Nefarith seems to break that rule by drawing on the Æther herself. Perlica's warning that history may repeat, and that no one like her has appeared in many years, implies such people existed before. This may suggest a link to the war that destroyed the first landing, mentioned in the prologue, but the text does not confirm it.

The Civilization Band is shown as a network of allied factions held together by shared technology. The Cabal of Tranquility speaks in religious terms, with relic scripts of ancient knowledge, written confessions and a Latin-named display piece, the Sanctilamina Cathedralis Tranquillae. Possibly the Cabal descends from Laterano, the church state of the original Arknights, but nothing in the text says so. A Sarkaz sits on the General Technological Committee, and the Sarkaz are a Terran people, which confirms again that Terra's races settled Talos-II. The recap also names the United Syndicates, whose fury Crowe calls down to turn the final battle.

The Endmin's legend comes into focus. They built the Dijiang, its Control Nexus responds only to them, and people remember them as the one in the Sarcophagus, a figure who faded into story during the ten-year sleep. In the original Arknights, the Doctor is found sleeping in a sarcophagus with no memory at the start of the story, and the parallel here is plain. This may suggest that the Endministrator is the Doctor, or that Endfield's story deliberately echoes theirs. The recap also shows how far the Endmin will go, nearly destroying themselves to stop Nefarith, and that the next threat, the Very Large Rift, lies at Wuling.

happened: Path of Ascension opens with the landslide toward the Originium Science Park nearly cleared. Shawna thanks the Endministrator for her rescue, and Director Qin Jiangchi explains what is at stake on the Power Plateau: the Originium Power Plant that keeps all of Valley IV powered, and the UWST Æther Test Site that has long monitored a quasi-permanent Æther rift there. Radio interference has cut all contact with the plateau. Then the rift erupts and Blight spreads across the region. Perlica suspects Nefarith deliberately energized it. Andre offers a way out: the TA-TA Prototype, a machine built to stabilize Æther fluctuations, which he adjusts so it can also expose Blight Cores. The Endmin, Perlica and Chen Qianyu must escort it to the plateau.

At the Science Park sentry post, Fabian Collins of the UWST Security Bureau checks the team, guessing at their races and taking Chen for a Vouivre until she insists she is a Lung. The Endmin is missing from his database but cleared by his superiors. He warns that the Landbreakers shrugged off energy cannon fire and asks the team to look for his colleague Aleeza. Chen names the Prototype Tata, and its emotes show it has opinions of its own. Its first scan exposes a Blight Core but leaves it overheating, and it settles only under the Endmin's touch. The team frees Aleeza, who turns out to be Fabian's younger sister. She lends them the Park's access card and praises Yvonne, a scientist whose defenses saved many workers. Once the gate is powered, the siblings head back in to find the missing, since the United Syndicates leaves no one behind.

Deeper in, Yvonne's booming broadcasts, laser traps and bomber drones keep the Landbreakers at bay, though they also trap the workers she gathered underground. With most paths flooded by Blight, the Endmin realizes that Techno-Protocol can link Tata to a Protocom Signal Tower and widen its scan. It works, but the heat nearly melts Tata's casing. Yvonne, waiting in her Research Center lab, turns out to be Tata's creator, helped by Andre, and calls it her baby bot. She explains that it is an automated Arts Unit whose Originium energy pulse makes small rifts collapse, and scolds the team for pushing it so hard. After the Endmin picks her favorite vinyl, she repairs Tata at the platform by the back gate and stays behind to study the data from its first large scan.

On the road to the Origin Lodespring, Yvonne reports that she has upgraded Tata, and Chen notices wounds left by a master of the blade. Three Ankhors have fallen in the area, yet few Aggeloi roam it, and with the freight road destroyed the only way to the plateau is a shaft through the Cradle of the Ages, sealed for twenty years. A worker named Alia leads the team to Rossi, Rossina Wulfperl Luppino of the Pack and Wulfgard's younger sister, who has been taking the most dangerous rescue work for the Mining Camp. She is crushed to learn the Endmin has forgotten the legends she grew up with. At the camp, Medical Officer Yue directs relief, the shaken rescuer Alfass describes a woman who set off shockwaving Ankhors with a flick of her hand, and Royle explains that an Originium branch shielded him from the blasts.

Royle sends them to Granny Jenner, who has tended a living Originium sapling for twenty years. She tells how the Great Originium Oak once grew in the Cradle, planted by someone who promised the land would become a home, and how the giant Aggelos Astarron fell upon the Valley. The people won only by detonating the Oak, whose shards tore through Astarron's core, leaving its shattered body entombed in the hollow trunk. As she speaks, the Endmin hears a voice promising that the tree will protect them, and Perlica recognizes the sapling as the Endmin's own work. The Ankhors then stir, and the team fights off a sudden surge of Aggeloi while Tata, left in the camp with curious children, helps keep them safe.

The team then destroys the Ankhors one by one, finding each is tied to the barrier sealing the Cradle, and survives the shockwaves with Originium branches that respond to the Endmin. They rescue Royle's missing survey team, who were saved by the branches and glimpsed an Archosaurian woman Perlica takes to be Nefarith, and Tata's tower scan exposes the last Ankhor. Inside the Cradle they defeat the giant Aggelos. A new sapling sprouts from the Oak's stump, and beautiful Originium geodes cover the old scar. Perlica reflects that a choice the Endmin made long ago has opened a path for them now. On the eve of the final push, she admits she is looking for a way to keep the Endmin out of danger, while Chen poses for a photo with Tata.
lore: This process shows how the Æther threatens Talos-II. Director Qin explains that rifts are scattered across the planet, mostly invisible to the eye, and Perlica describes them as places where the Ætherside touches realspace and sets off Blight. Valley IV has a quasi-permanent rift that the UWST has studied for years at its Test Site. Tata is the human answer: an Arts Unit programmed with Originium Arts that make small rifts collapse. Nefarith, meanwhile, appears able to wake a dormant rift, and Perlica openly wonders whether she can also choose where Ankhors fall, a capability no one in Endfield's database has recorded.

The process also deepens the mystery of the Endministrator. The Endmin can shape Originium as no one else can: Perlica recognizes the Great Originium Oak, its sapling and the shockwave-blocking branches as the Endmin's work, and the branches respond to their touch. Rossi repeats legends that the Endmin unleashed Originium Arts a century ago and left the Aurora of Talos-II, shattered Talos-V by throwing it into the Ætherside, and wiped out two thousand Ankhors underground in one strike, leaving a crater on the surface. The Endmin remembers none of it, and Perlica's growing worry for their safety hints that these powers come at a cost.

Valley IV's own history is bound to the Endmin. The Oak's roots created the Originium veins that made the region rich, and an outpost grew around it as its planter foretold. Its destruction ended Astarron, the largest Aggelos in UWST records, and the Cradle has been sealed for some twenty years since. The process also shows the factions working side by side: the UWST runs mining camps and a Security Bureau that the workers trust completely, Medical Officer Yue comes from the Hongshan Academy of Sciences, and Rossi shows that the Pack, still sometimes mistaken for Landbreakers, are long-standing partners of Endfield.

Links to the original Arknights run through the text. The sentry sorts the team by races known from Terra, naming Liberi, Vouivre, Lung and Ægir, and the survey team calls Nefarith an Archosaurian. Originium, the crystal at the heart of Terra's world, is everywhere here, channelled through Arts Units and burned for power. Yet on Terra Originium is feared as the cause of Oripathy, while in Valley IV a living Originium tree is remembered as a protector and the source of the land's wealth. This may suggest that the Endmin, or the settlers of Talos-II, found ways of using Originium that were unknown on Terra.

happened: Smoking Embers takes the team onto the Power Plateau, where the Originium Power Plant, a symbol of the UWST's pioneering past, stands beside the Æther Test Site, a symbol of its future. Both are overrun. A radio call from Professor Matz Crowe, verified by comms officer Fiona, leads them first to his apprentice Angro, who is disabling the energy reservoir's safeties so its discharge can flatten the whole plateau. Crowe confirms the plan: evacuate the survivors, then die taking the Landbreakers with him, since he sees the plant as a fitting tomb. He changes his mind on seeing Tata, the Prototype he once handed over to Yvonne, and proposes another way.

That way is the Utjug Order, an Arts Unit kept at UWST resource sites that declares an area under destructive military assault and calls in every UWST military facility. It needs a signal emitter and two keycards held by the highest commanders, and Crowe is the only one left; the Order has not been considered since the giant Aggelos was blown up at the Origin Lodespring. The team finds the apprentice Dean with a bloodstained keycard taken from the body of Site Director Daniels, Crowe's old friend, then reaches Clavell, who sealed a Landbreaker inside the lab holding the emitter and trapped himself in the process. Meanwhile Crowe studies Tata, baffled that its algorithms seem to have learned on their own, and reminds the Endmin that they once saved this land.

Outside, with the Landbreakers massed around their denstacks, Crowe gives a fiery speech and sends the Order, demanding a bombardment of his own position. The younger commander who answers refuses, tells him his new mission is to protect his people and sends reinforcements instead, along with beacons the team can use to call artillery onto the denstacks. Crowe grudgingly accepts and puts Valley IV's hopes in the Prototype. At the gates of the Æther Test Site, the team reads symbols visible only through the haze to pass the mechanisms, and Perlica reminds everyone that the goal is to seal the rift, not to defeat Nefarith at any cost. With Tata in place, they go in for the final showdown.

When it is over, the rift is gone, but Tata is gone with it, and Chen blames herself. Perlica tells the Endmin that their body is struggling along with their memory, that only they know the whole Zeroth Directive, and that they never wanted victory at a devastating cost. She also notes that Nefarith escaped, and that her parting words suggested she knows the Endmin well. At the Hub Base, Andre, Director Qin and the defenders celebrate, and Qin presents a plan to restore the base within a season. Many Bonekrushers have left Valley IV, but Wulfgard notes they are withdrawing in good order rather than fleeing. Rossi asks to join the Crisis Team, Crowe thanks the Endmin, and the Collins siblings reveal they grew up reading about the Endmin in history lessons on the Aggeloi War.

Yvonne then gives the team a test component, powered by Protocol-Originium and amplified through their Protosyncs, that can find Blight Cores in small patches but cannot deal with rifts. Her analysis shows Nefarith used the rift's existing energy and cannot yet open rifts from nothing, and that this was Valley IV's worst Blight incident in ten years. Told of Tata's sacrifice, she takes it calmly and chooses to honor the lives it saved. While tracing a faint Æther signal with Tata's scan logs from the signal towers, the team learns that a giant Vouivre leading Landbreakers attacked the Power Plant and was driven off, and Perlica suspects Rhodagn has survived. Lycia, an ex-Endfielder and lone hunter who keeps a promise the Endmin made her, appears at the scene.

The process ends with the Conference of the Four, held from Dijiang. Perlica reports to the UWST, the Talos-II General Chamber of Commerce (TGCC) and the Hongshan Academy of Sciences (HAS) that the Zeroth Directive is being deliberately obstructed. The UWST orders the Bonekrushers hunted across the region; the TGCC says the Order of Steel Oath detected non-Aggeloid activity near a rift on the Northern Front; and HAS reports Æther-emitting tracks found in the south, warning that the great enemy of a century ago may be returning. Under the Band Accord, Endfield's special authority is restored. Afterward M3, an elite operator and fellow executor of the Zeroth Directive, reports traces matching Valley IV's at the Wuling Very Large Rift, and the team prepares to leave for Wuling.
lore: This process sketches the political order of Talos-II. The Civilization Band rests on the Band Accord between three powers: the United Workers' Syndicates of Talos II, speaking through its Central Ministerial Committee and backed by an Industrial Mothership; the Talos-II General Chamber of Commerce, whose spokesperson invites the Endmin to the free city of La Fantoma; and the Hongshan Academy of Sciences, affiliated with the Tianshi Bureau of Great Yan. Endfield is the fourth party, and the Accordatories can restore its authority across the Band. The Utjug Order shows the UWST as a militarized frontier power, though its younger officers would rather save lives than follow Crowe's scorched-earth retaliation.

The wider threat grows clearer. Perlica mentions two Aggeloi Wars, during which the Civilization Band secured Endfield's right to survive, and says some factions still dream of its destruction. The HAS representative fears that the great enemy of a century ago is preparing to return and that its vanguard has already come, pointing to non-Aggeloid signals on the Northern Front and tracks still giving off Æther in the south. M3 warns that if something in the Ætherside is struggling to return to the planet, Nefarith may be only a diversion, and that the enemy will see the Protocol Automation-Core as a thorn in its side.

The Endministrator's condition becomes a central mystery. Perlica says the Endmin always returns to hibernation after leading as a hero, and voices overheard as the Endmin wakes say the damage to their Originium is metaphysical, has nothing to do with the Sarcophagus, will only worsen with each awakening, and can be repaired only by the Endmin. Someone also hints that the Automated Industry Complex was built for more than industry, mentioning an Assimilated Universe and what the Protocol-Originium might find. Nefarith seems to know the Endmin personally, Lycia keeps a promise the Endmin made, and Tata's apparent self-learning puzzles even Crowe.

Ties to the original Arknights are light but present. The giant Landbreaker is called a Vouivre, one of Terra's races, and Arts Units and Originium-fueled power plants follow the technology of Terra. When the apprentices guess what the Utjug Order might summon, Clavell mentions the legendary Steam Knights; in the original Arknights, the Steam Knights were Victoria's famed armored knights. Possibly the name survives on Talos-II as a legend carried over from Terra, but the text does not explain it, and nothing in this process says how the people of Talos-II came from or relate to Terra.

happened: Aboard Dijiang, the Endministrator, Perlica and Chen Qianyu learn from the Intel Office that Nefarith's Bonekrushers are moving towards Wuling, while Æther depth readings are shifting all over the world. M3 has to stay focused on the north, so the team is short of people. Their liaison will be Zhuang Fangyi, the leader of Wuling and one of the Tianshi of Great Yan. Chen, who trained in Wuling for about a year and is returning for the first time since joining Endfield, knows her only as the youngest Viceroy of an HAS developmental district and the subject of wild rumours. Chen vows that Wuling will not suffer another Valley IV Incident, and explains the Blight Tide: a water-linked Blight that swells with the rivers' tides.

The landing goes wrong. The pod comes down off course, radio contact with Fiona breaks up and the SOW navigation fails, so Chen leads the way towards the powered rafts Wuling keeps for travellers. At a ferry point they meet Ardashir, a courteous young man who cannot read Yanese, says he comes from the Free City of Kjersch, and mentions that the companions he set out with are all gone. Perlica's database finds no match for him, only figures from Sargonian history and unrelated employees. In a bamboo grove whose trees seem to move, the group keeps losing and finding him. At the grove's edge he asks the Endmin whether they approve of their endeavour, gets a firm yes, and, once alone, says the Endmin has truly forgotten everything and so will not forgive them.

The Endmin next wakes in an unfamiliar place, facing an eye-patched girl whom Chen recognises as Tangtang, once an underchief and now Supreme Chief of Qingbo Stockade, a community of locals that Chen says includes many petty thieves. Perlica is missing. Ardashir turns up again, oddly unruffled, then disappears without a trace. Since neither fighting nor sneaking out seems wise, Chen suggests playing along: she claims Wuling threw her out (in truth she failed its trials) and that she has come back with her new boss to get even. Tangtang, who has her own grudge against the Watchguard captain Mi Fu, gladly takes them in, names the Endmin Darkmask, and leads them to Perlica, who is in a standoff with Tangtang's older brother and first mate, Ruan Yi, after knocking out his men in self-defence.

Tangtang privately tells a wary Ruan Yi that she wants the outsiders to repair the Stockade's failing waterwheels. Reunited, Perlica concludes that Nefarith is in Wuling with a mysterious ally, and the team accepts Tangtang's deal: help the Stockade, and she will open the road to Wuling City, cut off for two weeks. When Aggeloi, which the locals call splatters, attack, the team saves the injured Da Jiang, fixes a bridge with bottled lake water, and helps Stonefang, the Stockade's fin-hunter, Qingwu, a former city dweller who sheltered the residents, and the gatekeeper He Lao. Perlica notes that the Landbreakers here raise no denstacks or camps, and Ruan Yi says they seem to be waiting for something. After a rescue at a small reef, Tangtang declares the Stockade and Endfield united.

Tangtang gives the Endmin a Tangtang Cert, a stylised copy of her own name that her brother had someone write for her, as a promise of help, offers the Third Seat of her family, and blows a wall open to reach the city. Mi Fu, captain of the Wuling Watchguards, arrives; Tangtang escapes, but Mi Fu already knows Chen's situation and goes to report. Chen explains the two women's constant feud, which mirrors that of Wuling and the Stockade, and Perlica recalls that Ardashir seemed to hold authority over Nefarith. The blast has jammed the gate of the Field Logistics Depot, a decade-old structure built jointly by HAS and Endfield, so the team revives an obsolete Jia-type jet drone to turn its bearings. Mi Fu leaves to make an arrest, noting that her boss prefers the title Tianshi to Viceroy.
lore: This process introduces Wuling, a city of Great Yan within HAS, run by Tianshi, its trained officials and specialists (the text mentions a Tianshi Bureau, Tianshi interns and Tianshi engineers). Yan is also the name of a great nation on Terra in the original Arknights, and Chen Qianyu, called a Lung by Tangtang, belongs to the same draconic people as Arknights' Ch'en of Lungmen. The text does not explain how Talos-II's Great Yan relates to Terra's Yan. Possibly it was founded by settlers who carried that nation's name and culture to the new world, but the process only shows a Yanese language, Yanese technology and a strong local identity.

Ardashir is the arc's central mystery. He claims to come from Kjersch, a free city ringed by snowy mountains, and the only records of his name belong to Sargonian history; Sargon is a desert nation of Terra in the original game. This may suggest a link to Terra's past, and Kjersch may echo Kjerag, the snowy mountain realm of the original game, though the text names neither connection. This may suggest, from his parting words, that he knew the Endministrator before their memory loss and that he and others did something the Endmin would not forgive. Perlica also recalls that he seemed to exercise authority over Nefarith.

The arc also sketches Wuling's divided society. Qingbo Stockade survives outside the city's protection, scorned as bandits, short of food and resentful of Wuling, yet Chen insists neither side truly wants the other gone. HAS and Endfield, Perlica says, have worked together for longer than Wuling City has existed, This may suggest that Endfield's roots on Talos-II, and the Endmin's own role in them, run very deep. Familiar Arknights terms recur: Originium Arts, Arts Units used by casters, and races such as the Liberi and Feline. Perlica notes that the Landbreakers behave nothing like they did in Valley IV and suspects they have secret plans.

happened: Outside Wuling, the team helps watchguards evacuate the merchant Pu Yuan and frightened farmers as Aggeloi strike. They then see Zhuang Fangyi flying above the Tianshi Pillar array, wielding the Thunder Arts that Chen says few in HAS can match, and Chen wonders why the city's leader would step in herself. A receptionist bot leads them down busy Fangxing Avenue, past a giant Chubby Lung mascot, where Chen meets old acquaintances such as Tianshi Lian Xiaowu of the Bureau of Swordmancers and Tianshi Ge Yipu. Chen is tense about coming back, and Perlica eases it by having her shout towards the city. At the Main Pillar, Mi Fu hands the Endmin a key to her boss's office and admits she let Tangtang go to deal with something urgent.

Zhuang Fangyi greets the Endmin warmly and, seeing their memory loss, reveals they met years ago when the Endmin visited the Wuling Science Station and gave her, then a Tianshi intern, personal guidance. She explains that several Tianshi Pillars were destroyed in the past week, and Perlica notes that Ardashir's Arts fit no modern framework and that he speaks an obscure language, which Zhuang wonders might be ancient Sargonian. A Xiranite sandbox shows overlapping tides flooding the outskirts: the pillars burn Xiranite so fast that reserves will last three months at most, and only an Automated Industry Complex can mass-produce more. When the Endmin touches the office's Xiranite beams, they respond, because Xiranite was born from a vision the Endmin shared with HAS. Zhuang hopes the city will bring back the Endmin's memories of a time when everyone was still around.

Zhuang explains that every habitable zone on Talos-II is hard-won, and that Wuling refuses to give up its food, trade and culture even inside the Blight Tide, though she saves the deeper story of the city's birth for later. The nervous trainee watchguard Lifeng guides the team to the industrial site, meeting Tianshi Yan Ning, head of the Xiranite application unit, and her student Bai Shuang. Aggeloi from an Ankhor deep in the tide have slipped inside the array, because pillars were switched off to save Xiranite. The PAC is dropped from Dijiang. When new data shows the Blight spreading faster than expected, Yan Ning angrily presses Zhuang about how bad the reserves really are and accuses her of carrying everything alone, then asks the Endmin to help her. Before heading to the laboratory, the team repairs a collapsed irrigation canal with the AIC Factory.

At the Xiranite Central Laboratory, the Endmin helps Zhuang, Ge Yipu and Chang Yun through a calibration test that keeps failing. Passing a blooming pear tree, Zhuang reveals that the city's first pear sapling was the Endmin's gift, with a promise of a future orchard. A runaway sky pole drone meant for a festival performance then drags them through Fangxing Avenue, past a crying child promised a special Chubby Lung, and into a hot pot at Da Pan's eatery before it crashes into a lamp post. Zhuang admits she wanted the Endmin to walk Wuling as a wanderer rather than a strategist, and shares the question that made her join the Science Expedition, written by a Tumu Tianshi in an old book: whether the young will still see green hills and rivers. The test then succeeds, opening the way to PAC-compatible Xiranite facilities.

Zhuang shows the Endmin the data room holding their old files, but is unsatisfied when she asks what the Endmin thinks of Wuling, before Perlica reports the production blueprints are ready. With Yan Ning's help the team builds the Forge of the Sky, and its first batch of Xiranite restores a Xiranite flow control node. An emergency follows: a Blight monitoring center has been overrun. Mi Fu has caught Tangtang again, and after losing a bet Tangtang agrees to help, then challenges Mi Fu to a count of slain Aggeloi that ends in a tie. Inside, Mi Fu charges the Aggelos Tidalklast alone and is wounded in the fight that follows; Tangtang fusses over her, and Mi Fu asks them not to tell Zhuang. Tangtang, plainly hiding a worry, asks for the AIC Factory to protect the Stockade, though she must first win over her brother and family.

Back in the office, Zhuang laments that the scars of a disaster ten years ago still divide Wuling from the Stockade, but sees Endfield as a chance to change that, and Perlica promises to seek balance between them. Zhuang adds that the Yinglung Special Task Force is tied up in the North Wuling Exclusion Zone, and that conditions across Talos-II are poor, reminding her of ten years ago. In the final mission Tangtang meets the team on the pretext of escorting them, really wanting a bridge repaired. The Stockade welcomes Darkmask warmly, and the AIC Factory begins with a farm complex. Tangtang mentions that some residents have been sneaking in and out and that her brother is always busy, and promises a tour of the Ancestral Spring. Elsewhere, Ardashir muses that someone accepted but did not agree, and wonders how to proceed without too many sacrifices.
lore: This process is the main source on Xiranite, the foundation of Wuling. It is an Originium derivative, described as Protocol-Originium given extra properties by the Forge, and an offshoot of the Protorig technology behind Endfield's AIC. It was meant to seal rifts, stop the Blight and cleanse land and water, and it took Wuling over a decade to simplify its manufacture enough to mass-produce it as the city's core. Originium is the central mineral of the original Arknights, the source of Arts and of the disease Oripathy; on Talos-II it is also an industrial base. That Xiranite still responds to the Endmin, and that the Endmin first envisioned it, ties the Endmin's past to this technology, echoing Valley IV, where the Great Originium Oak stirred the Endmin's memories.

Wuling's history begins to surface. It grew from the Wuling Science Station and a Science Expedition built at the edge of danger, and a disaster ten years ago broke trust between the city and Qingbo Stockade. Chen speaks of thirty years of Endfield reports, and Zhuang recalls a hopeful time when everyone, the Endmin included, was still around. This may suggest that people close to the Endmin and to Wuling's founding were lost or scattered, but the process does not say how. Zhuang's remarks that habitable zones on Talos-II are precious, and that the planet as a whole is in trouble, frame Wuling as one fragile outpost of the Civilization Band.

The threats deepen. Ardashir's Arts fall outside any modern Originium framework and Perlica calls his language more esoteric than ancient Sargonian. This may suggest he draws on a different time, tradition or source of power. Possibly this connects him to the ancient powers of the Arknights universe, but the text does not say so. The Blight here is waterborne, fed by an Ankhor inside the tide, and the attack on the monitoring center looks deliberate. His closing remark, that someone accepted but did not agree, hints at a deal with someone close to the story; possibly this points to the Stockade, where residents are slipping away. The Yinglung Special Task Force and the North Wuling Exclusion Zone are introduced as HAS's front against a wider danger.

happened: The process opens with Wuling under attack from its own neighbours. Masked Stockaders slip into the monitoring center during a watchguard shift change and sabotage its comms, while another group strikes the Field Logistics Depot, wounding watchguards and trying to burn it down. The Endministrator, Perlica and Chen Qianyu drive them off but recognize none of them, and Tangtang, Chief of Qingbo Stockade, is not answering calls. Zhuang Fangyi promises to keep Wuling calm and quietly leaves the matter to Endfield. At the depot, Mi Fu, captain of the Wuling Watchguards, agrees to go into the Stockade with them, warning that ten years of bad blood between Stockade and City could end badly. The Stockade gate stays shut, so Mi Fu leads them in through a little-known secret passage.

Inside, the Stockade is strangely quiet, with no denstacks or Landbreaker camps. A captured Stockader, terrified of Mi Fu, points them toward Tangtang's cell, and the friends they free, Lang Tou and Stonefang, explain that an uprising has taken place: Stockaders jealous of Tangtang's profitable partnership with Wuling began holding night meetings once outsiders arrived, jailed everyone who refused to join, and detained both Tangtang and her brother Ruan Yi. Waterbell, who admires Ruan Yi, slips off alone to find him. Mi Fu reveals she herself came from the Stockade and explains the feud: ten years ago an Ætherside disaster struck the Wuling Science Station, the Stockade suffered Blight Tides and Aggelos attacks, and many Stockaders blamed the outsiders. Ruan Yi's father, she was told, was killed by the Tianshi.

Fighting through Stockaders who want a war of revenge, the team reaches Tangtang's cell just as Ardashir leads Ruan Yi away to the Ancestral Spring, telling him he has yet to master his new powers and that hatred never builds anything great. Tangtang wakes from a nightmare of the rainy night in her childhood when Ruan Yi's father died and her eye was wounded, and insists on chasing her brother. Mi Fu, bound by duty, leaves to report to Zhuang Fangyi and put Wuling on alert, asking the Endmin to keep Tangtang alive. Though the Endmin does not share Tangtang's belief that Ruan Yi is being forced, they promise, as Darkmask, Occupant of the Third Seat of Qingbo Stockade, to stand with their Chief whatever the truth turns out to be.

The truth grows harder to deny. Near the Spring they find weapons, explosives and plans of Wuling prepared well in advance, then Waterbell, gravely wounded by Ruan Yi himself, who begs Tangtang not to hate him. Two fleeing Stockaders, Rusty Hook and Iron Boatswain, help fix a rusted bridge in exchange for being allowed to escape. At the Ancestral Spring Ruan Yi waits alone, his arm visibly affected by the power he is trying to master. He calls this his only chance at revenge and asks the Endmin to take Tangtang somewhere far away, yet he also turns on Ardashir, whose voice warns him that he is not ready and will die. Ruan Yi dies, and Chen feels he gave up at the very end. Ardashir later appears to pay his respects, insisting that everything he does is for the survival of Civilization.

Tangtang then reveals the past: she was adopted, Ruan Yi was her father's real son, and ten years ago, with people in the Stockade starving, the two men raided a Wuling supply convoy. The Tianshi, shaken by the disaster in the Exclusion Zone, fought back, and in the rain her father was killed and her eye injured. The Endmin trades one of her Tangtang Certs for her promise to keep going, and she resolves to settle the matter as Chief. Meanwhile Nefarith and Ardashir prepare to disable the Xiranite Dam, Nefarith boasting she can tear open the Very Large Rift at any moment. In the Stockade, Ruan Yi's loyalists, led by his old advisor Uncle Shang, who lost his own child in that raid, now want revenge on both Tangtang and Wuling. Tangtang spares Dirt Rinser after an ambush but tries to handle the rest alone.

Through her aide Qingwu, the Endmin learns Tangtang is secretly hunting four loyalists inside Wuling. After a comic mix-up with the hot pot owner Da Pan, she finds a bomb in an underground canal; the Endmin covers for her in front of Mi Fu and disarms it, and Tangtang finally accepts help. Tracking Dirt Rinser through thick fog to a hideout near the Ancestral Spring, they see Stockaders joining the Landbreakers, find Ruan Yi's secret room holding a Tianshi apparatus kept with her father's belongings, and defeat Uncle Shang, who agrees to a truce to drive the Landbreakers out. Tangtang buries Ruan Yi's horn by the Spring, then meets Zhuang Fangyi, who accepts her terms to pardon the Stockaders and offers aid. On the way home Tangtang agrees to visit Endfield and look for her own answers.
lore: This process shows that the feud between Qingbo Stockade and Wuling City is a split within one people. Mi Fu stresses that both descend from Yanese pioneers, and Tangtang notes they share the same speech and traditions. The apparatus in Ruan Yi's room bears Stockade carvings added later over an older maker's mark, the Tianshi Bureau of Shangshu of Great Yan, and the Endmin judges it to be neither a Wuling nor a HAS design. In the original Arknights, Yan is the great East Asian-inspired nation of Terra. This may suggest that the Yanese settlers of Talos-II brought tools from Terra's Yan, and that Tangtang's father had Tianshi ancestry, which would make the Stockade and the City branches of the same founding community.

The disaster of ten years ago sits at the center of everything. It struck the Wuling Science Station and the area now called the Exclusion Zone, set off famine and Aggelos attacks in the Stockade, and turned a convoy raid into a killing that shaped Ruan Yi's whole life. Perlica adds that it happened at the same time as the Polar Expedition and the Endministrator's last awakening, and that disasters across the Civilization Band drove many people to tragedies like his. This may suggest the Endmin's own history is tied to that event in ways not yet explained.

Ardashir and Nefarith also come into sharper focus. Perlica notes that Ardashir is not a Bonekrusher yet can give Nefarith orders, and that Nefarith now works toward a concrete goal under a higher command, quietly gathering strength instead of fighting Wuling head-on. Ardashir gives Ruan Yi a dangerous new power that leaves the land around the Spring ravaged, then speaks of predator and prey, creator and creation, and of acting for the survival of Civilization. Their stated aim is to disable the Xiranite Dam and open the Very Large Rift. His remark that it pains him to see the Endmin's expression again may suggest he knew the Endministrator long before this meeting.

Smaller details tie Talos-II to Terra's peoples: Mi Fu is called a pink-haired Sarkaz, one of the original Arknights' races, and Tangtang thanks Talos the way Terrans might invoke a god. The process also shows how the Landbreakers spread, by moving into communities already torn by grief and resentment rather than by conquest. Even Ruan Yi's own loyalists split over it: Dirt Rinser and Uncle Shang opposed bringing in outsiders, calling their quarrel with Wuling personal, while others joined anyone who would help them strike the City.

happened: After Ardashir attacks the Marker Stone, Zhuang Fangyi explains that it is the origin of the Xiranite Dam and of Wuling City itself, raised by generations of Tianshi around a creation that HAS persuaded a Feranmut Proxy to leave there. Unable to leave the city, she grants the Endministrator full command of the Marker Stone area and assigns Arcane, the youngest major in Wuling's service and youngest task leader of the Yinglung Special Task Force (YSTF), whose unit has just left its posts in the North Wuling Exclusion Zone. Chen Qianyu seems uneasy at the name. Perlica worries about the Endmin, who forced not-yet-recovered powers against Nefarith and was saved only by a suppressor, and notes that even Endfield's clearance under the Band Accord turns up nothing on Ardashir.

Arcane, whom Chen calls Li, rescues the Tianshi Xi Mo from a strange Blight-like entity and formally hands field command to the Endmin. Her blunt, by-the-book manner grates on Chen, who admits she was a YSTF reservist after Tanjian Hall, hoped to become a heroic fighter like her mother, failed, and fought with Arcane. At the Security Section Arcane draws on a Feranmut Heart, a vessel that preserves a Feranmut's power, and shares intel: Ardashir's fire matches no Originium Arts theory and behaves like Æther. When hostile activity hits Cloudrest Woods, the Endmin chooses to save people first. There Ardashir has disabled a Tianshi Pillar and torn open a rift; Arcane breaks his Arts and restarts the Pillar, and the team suspects the attack was a feint meant to draw the Endmin in.

At Lake Islet a talking entity speaks with Ardashir's voice, and at the Marker Stone entrance he raises an Ætherside barrier of phantom swords and walls. He says his targets are the Very Large Rift and the Endministrator, and offers to talk Nefarith out of violence if the Endmin leads the Wulingers away from the Rift. The Endmin replies that he has no right to tell people to leave their homes, and senses having seen such phantoms before. While activating the auxiliary pillars they find Rusty Hook and Iron Boatswain, trapped after sneaking through an old raid tunnel to visit their grandfather's relic. Arcane wants to eliminate them, but the Endmin and Chen let them go; Arcane says only that she does not question the Endmin's orders.

Inside, Ardashir mocks the Endmin as a weakened shadow who still cradles the fate of Terra, announces that he will destroy the Marker Stone so the Very Large Rift reveals the whole Ætherside, and teleports to its tip. The Feranmut Proxy's ink spirits guide the team to the Xirancore Jades needed to restart a damaged Feranmut Heart, and the Proxy lends Arcane greater control over the Marker Stone. Arcane, wondering whether Ardashir is even human, offers herself as a trump card, admitting her chances of getting out are poor. Chen protests, and the Endmin orders the team to face Ardashir together; Arcane says she understands.

Passing through the scroll, the Endmin finds themself alone before an intact Feranmut Heart, in a place they once saw in a dream. Ardashir, crediting the power of the Feranmut Sui, talks about himself: a cliffside home in Kjersch above a snowy valley of headstones for those who died for him, another home of gold and sand beyond the Cosmic Gate where he was called Pasha, and a long life bought by stealing the lives of those he held dear. He wants to open the Very Large Rift to find the Exiles in the Ætherside, names the Foundation, which the Endmin recognizes as the force behind the likes of him, gives the Endmin a favourite dinar and invites them back to the place beneath the aurora's crown. The Endmin refuses.

Arcane then seals Ardashir inside the scroll along with herself. Depth readings return to normal, and Zhuang Fangyi says Arcane should hold out until the Sui Regulator steps in. Xi Mo and Ge Yipu of the Institute of Materials Science guide the Endmin in setting up the AIC Factory to make Heavy Xiranite and repair the Feranmut Heart, and the two Stockader brothers are given lodging. Chen searches Sui Regulator files for a way into the scroll and explains she was disqualified from the YSTF for immaturity of mind. The Endmin predicts Nefarith will move next, and the process ends with a Landbreaker telling Nefarith that Ardashir's plan has failed, and her reply that it is time to begin.
lore: This process brings the Feranmuts into the story. Perlica describes the Sui Regulator as a special HAS body above the YSTF, closely tied to mysterious Terran entities called Feranmuts, and Arcane calls the Feranmut Heart a technology from the Age of Terra, joined with Protocol-Originium tech. Ardashir names the power behind the scroll as the Feranmut Sui, and the Proxy, whose physical form is far from Wuling, helps through ink spirits. In the original Arknights, Sui is the ancient colossal being of Yan whose fragments became Nian, Dusk, Ling and their siblings. This may suggest that Sui's power reached Talos-II with the Yanese settlers. Possibly the painted scroll worlds recall Dusk, the painter among those fragments, but the text never names the Proxy.

Ardashir's account of himself is the process's biggest reveal. He has lived for over a century, once had a home on the far side of the Cosmic Gate in an arrogant empire of gold and sand where he was called Pasha, and kept himself alive by taking the lives of people he loved. He calls humans Terrans as if he were not one, and Arcane openly doubts he is human. This may suggest the Cosmic Gate is the link between Talos-II and Terra. Possibly Kjersch and the sand empire echo Terra's Kjerag and Sargon from the original Arknights, but the text does not say so.

The Endministrator's forgotten past also deepens. Arcane says the Endmin was once a symbol that meant different things to different people, enemies included; Ardashir speaks of the Endmin's vestigial powers, the Exiles in the Ætherside, the Foundation, and a place beneath the aurora's crown he calls the origin of all life. He also speaks of the final lord he served and pleads for a change of ways. This may suggest the Endmin was once that lord, and that the Endmin's old war with these forces is part of what Ardashir wants to undo. Possibly the aurora points to the polar regions, but nothing confirms it.

Finally, the process explains how Wuling holds back the Rift: Xiranite was made to fill rifts and cancel out Æther, the Marker Stone anchors the Xiranite Dam over the Very Large Rift, and Ardashir is the first person anyone has seen wield Æther like Originium Arts, even tearing new rifts. The two Stockader brothers' claim of Tianshi descent again hints that Qingbo and Wuling share roots.

happened: The process opens in the middle of the Landbreaker assault on Wuling City. At the Tianshi Pillar Array, Chang Yun reports that the surging Blight Tide and the rampaging Landbreakers have overloaded the Array Cores, and Perlica reasons that the Heavy Xiranite Zhuang Fangyi arranged can repair the cores as well as reinforce them. Once the first core holds, the team sees trouble in the Institute's direction. With Dijiang unable to verify coordinates, Perlica uses the PAC position she memorised and sets up Zipline Pylons so the Endministrator, Perlica and Chen Qianyu can cross the city quickly. There Ge Yipu explains that Nefarith has set the array floor ablaze with Æther flames like those at the Marker Stone, which are nearly impossible to put out. Da Pan arrives with townsfolk who refused to hide in shelters and builds an aerial route over the fire to the core.

With that core repaired, the Tianshi and locals stay on watch, and the thunder of Zhuang Fangyi's Lei Fa draws the team to the main gate, where she is fighting beside the watchguards. Zhuang brings good and bad news. HAS received their message before the signal dropped and will interfere with the Marker Stone Scroll remotely to help Arcane chase Ardashir, so they must trust the Sui Regulator. But Wuling City is on its own. Nefarith commands the Blight itself and can strike the Xiranite Dam directly, making her a danger to Wuling and to the whole Civilization Band. Zhuang insists they stop her here, saying this time Wuling and Endfield are in it together, and sends the Endmin to reinforce the three Array Cores with Heavy Xiranite.

Zhuang's real plan is a trap. If the array holds back the Blight Tide, and the Marker Stone still holds enough Feranmut power to seal Ardashir, then with the Endmin and the Tianshi far away on the battlefield Nefarith's best move is to strike the Main Pillar. Over Perlica's protest that this is far too risky, Zhuang reveals that the Main Pillar, the heart of Wuling and its palace of Xiranite, is her most expensive trap. Nefarith takes the bait, first moving on the Core AIC Area to destroy the source of Xiranite, then leaping across the city toward the Main Pillar. Chen wants to rush to Zhuang's side, but Mi Fu tells her to stay on the core: the array protects every Wulinger, that is the cause her Boss defends, and her Boss is stronger than they think.

Mi Fu and Tangtang hold the line together so the Endmin can repair the last core. Tangtang, who calls the Endmin Darkmask, declares that Nefarith owes Qingbo Stockade a blood debt. With the Tianshi Pillar Array running again and the city shielded for a while, Mi Fu tells the Endmin they are the only one who can help Zhuang, and the Endmin promises not to let her fight alone. In the next mission the Blight Tide ebbs and the hunt for Nefarith that began in Valley IV is over. An exhausted Zhuang admits she felt a measure of relief when Nefarith attacked the Main Pillar, since her only real fear was for Wuling, and the Xiranite Dam still stands. Perlica expects the Bonekrushers and Stockade turncoats to scatter, while Chen wonders why Nefarith and Ardashir are so obsessed with the Ætherside.

On an inspection tour, Physician Cui reports many injured but says ten years of crises have made their procedures solid, and Watchguard Liu says the citizens already have a mahjong game going. At the Marker Stone Flats, Summit of the Yinglung Special Task Force reports seventeen enemy leaders down; most of the Cangzei Pirates surrendered, which Zhuang corrects to Stockaders, while the Landbreakers retreated in good order, so an enemy commander likely remains. The Sui Regulator is sending one person, not a Tianshi, who has already used the scroll's residual power to rescue Arcane. Arcane lies unconscious in a special room of the Main Pillar, brought out by an Ink Spirit, with no visible wounds; Summit blames the strain of her Originium Arts. Zhuang senses something is wrong, and Chen wonders whether Ardashir ever fought back inside the scroll.

Visiting the wounded, Zhuang finds Lifeng shaken by his first real battle and unsure his parents would want this for him; she tells him to keep his doubts and go see the rest of the city. Li Zhui held three Aggeloi away from the Bureau of Swordmancers and saved two citizens. On Fangxing Avenue, Zhuang asks Da Pan whether she chose rightly, and he tells her she never had a choice and to drop the maybes, then quietly asks the Endmin to walk the path with her. Zhuang asks Endfield to stay as guests and rest, though Perlica notes their mission, Project Xiranite and the Wuling Very Large Rift, is unfinished. The Endmin makes her promise to look after herself. Mi Fu scolds Zhuang for playing bait without her, and Zhuang thanks the volunteers, Tangtang among them, hiding nearby.
lore: This process shows how completely Wuling rests on Xiranite. The Tianshi Pillar Array is Xiranite-based, Heavy Xiranite can both reinforce and repair its cores, the Xiranite Dam holds back the Blight, and Zhuang calls the Main Pillar the palace of Xiranite. Because Nefarith commands the Blight itself and can strike the Dam, Zhuang treats her as a threat to the entire Civilization Band, not only to one city, which suggests Wuling's Xiranite matters far beyond its walls. Physician Cui's remark about ten years of crisis procedures and Zhuang's line that this time is different from ten years ago both point back to a past disaster that the next process explores.

The battle also maps Wuling's allies and enemies. HAS can reach into the Marker Stone Scroll from afar, the Sui Regulator acts through a single envoy who is not a Tianshi, and the Yinglung Special Task Force must hurry back to the North Wuling Exclusion Zone. The Landbreakers retreat in order and leave the turncoat Stockaders behind as pawns, and Zhuang pointedly calls the captives Stockaders rather than Cangzei Pirates, keeping faith with the peace she made with Qingbo Stockade. Several mysteries stay open: why Nefarith and Ardashir care so much about the Ætherside, whether Ardashir resisted Arcane at all, who is still commanding the enemy, and the Exiles, whom the Endmin can bring up in a reply.

The clearest link to the original Arknights is vocabulary. Summit speaks of Arcane's Originium Arts, the term Arknights uses for arts cast through Originium, and the cost they take on her body echoes how Arts are portrayed there. Wuling's culture, with its Tianshi, Lei Fa, mahjong and hotpot, follows the Yanese style that the outline ties to the city's founders, and Yan is an eastern nation on Terra in the original game. Possibly the Sui Regulator, the Feranmut power in the Marker Stone and the Ink Spirit that carried Arcane out of the scroll echo the Sui of Arknights' Yan, but the text itself makes no such connection.

happened: With Nefarith defeated and Wuling rebuilding, Zhuang Fangyi meets the Endministrator at the Marker Stone Flats. The AIC Factory has restored Xiranite production, the Tianshi Pillar Array works again, Mi Fu is handling city repairs and Tangtang her Stockade, yet the lantern that symbolises Wuling's peace is still dark. The aftershocks of Nefarith's blow, which Zhuang blocked, compromised the Xiranite Dam, and a new rift has opened beneath the city. Using her highest authority, Zhuang takes the Endmin down to the Underground Array, now a chaotic labyrinth. The Pillar at full power keeps the rift from growing, but Wuling cannot be safe while it remains. She explains the Xiranite Nexus, a rift-sealing device whose development stalled and which only the Endmin can help finish. Nearby, a scroll portal preserves traces of the Wuling Science Station from ten years ago, until rising Æther forces them out.

Waiting in Zhuang's office, the Endmin notices a calendar of work running deep into the night, a note from Mi Fu telling her to eat, and a fresh order of 24 energy drinks; Zhuang insists she is properly rested. At the Xiranite Central Laboratory, the Xiranite Forge's pressure valve has failed, trapping the Nexus, which had become a component of the Forge after the project stopped. Chang Yun wants engineers to dismantle the old Forge and Ge Yipu reluctantly agrees, but Zhuang and the Endmin rewrite the valve's command script instead. Zhuang explains the Nexus's flaws: it consumed vast amounts of Xiranite, no longer a problem, and it seals rifts by brute force, its sudden release of Xiranite energy reacting with Æther and causing unpredictable losses. The Endmin has an idea but needs surface Blight Tide data. In her office sits a ten-year-old Bamboo Brew, still sealed.

At the monitoring center with Mi Fu, the data supports a bold refinement that cuts Xiranite consumption further. Zhuang recalls the Science Station team's fierce debates, which she listened to as its youngest member while sorting their files, and Mi Fu remarks it is the first time anyone has kept pace with her wild ideas. For safety they test at Qijian Dais, an empty islet. There they find Lifeng paying respects to his parents, who trained him there and died in the accident ten years ago. He apologises to them for having been a clingy child who wanted them always beside him, and the Endmin tells him remembering them is not selfish. While he guards the raft station, the test succeeds, and Zhuang recalls how Tianshi Li and his wife used to invite her along, saying Lifeng takes after their dutiful, fearless nature.

Before they can seal the rift, two calls split them up: a defense system upgrade at the Bureau of Swordmancers is throwing errors, and Mi Fu reports the injured are waking. They agree to meet at the lab. The Endmin spends a long time fixing an Endfield-made torque module for the Bureau's Tianshi and turns down their eager questions. Meanwhile Zhuang visits Uncle Zhao, whose daughter, who dreamed of training under her, is gravely injured. Seeing the Endmin surrounded by Tianshi, Zhuang reproaches herself for selfishness and leaves with the Nexus alone. She leaves behind a consent form naming no other investigators, a handover giving city affairs to Mi Fu and Academy matters to Ge Yipu, health reports far below healthy standards, and an application on which many Tianshi had volunteered and she simply wrote that she would go.

Her letter to the Endmin apologises for breaking her promise. She writes that her negligence endangered Wuling, that seeing a project of more than a decade fulfil its purpose is a Tianshi's lifetime wish, and that if this is her final stop it should be their starting point for the push into the North Wuling Exclusion Zone. She remembers watching the Endmin from the crowd when they first visited the Science Station and stammering when she finally spoke to them; a decade later only the two of them remain from that crowd. The Endmin, she writes, is destined for greater burdens. But the Endmin reaches the Underground Array first, calls her claim to manage alone a lie, and insists they do it together, while the voices of Yan Ning, Ge Yipu, Lian Xiaowu and Mi Fu echo in her thoughts.

With the path destroyed, they pass through the scroll portal, which holds impressions the Science Station left in Zhuang's memory, preserved by the Proxy's power. They watch young Zhuang arrive as the youngest Tianshi of HAS and catch her senior's test, a fowlbeast egg study hidden in a paper; the announcement of the first Xiranite, as colleagues imagine her Xiranite city with hotpot, a plaza and a school at its most important place, all of which now exist in Wuling; and her despair on learning everyone died, when the Endmin speaks comfort to the memory. They pass the last surviving monitoring station and seal the rift together. The Endmin admits a fear that those who walked with them will leave, and Zhuang promises she won't leave easily. The lantern is lit, and she finally opens the Bamboo Brew with an old friend.
lore: This process reveals the origin of Xiranite and of Wuling itself. Xiranite was first made at the Wuling Science Station, where HAS headquarters sent Zhuang as its youngest Tianshi, and a voice from her past calls Wuling's completion essential to the Academy. The city grew out of the science team's jokes about the Xiranite city they would build, school and plaza included. An accident ten years ago destroyed most of the station and killed the whole team except Zhuang, Lifeng's parents among them, leaving her to carry Project Xiranite and become Viceroy. Her letter frames the coming push into the North Wuling Exclusion Zone as the next step. This may suggest that the old disaster is tied to the Exclusion Zone and the Very Large Rift.

The Endministrator's own past runs through the story. Zhuang remembers the Endmin visiting the Science Station, says they were away when Xiranite was announced but congratulated the team, and writes that the two of them are the only ones left from that crowd. The Endmin admits to having slept while others kept going and waking without memories, and inside the scroll can energise inert Xiranite so Zhuang can move it, which fits the earlier statement that Xiranite was tied to the Endmin from the start. Possibly the Endmin's role in Project Xiranite was larger than Zhuang states here, since the text only shows them as a respected figure the team kept informed.

The process also clarifies how Wuling fights the Æther. Xiranite powers the Pillar Array and Dam, but released all at once it reacts with Æther and causes unpredictable losses, so a rift beneath an inhabited city needs a careful seal rather than brute force. The Proxy's power keeps memories alive inside a scroll, and under strong Æther the scroll's space blends with the real Underground Array. In the original Arknights, the protagonist known as the Doctor also wakes with amnesia and must rebuild ties with people who remember them. This may suggest a deliberate parallel with the Endmin, and possibly the Proxy's painted scrolls echo the Sui of Arknights' Yan, but this process names neither Terra nor Rhodes Island.

happened: While the Xiranite Nexus is tuned aboard Dijiang, Perlica and Zhuang Fangyi make the Endministrator rest, since the Endmin has not stopped working since peace returned to Wuling. The Endmin wakes from an unsettling dream to good news: the Nexus is calibrated and Arcane, rescued from the scroll, is awake. Arcane reports that her Originium Arts failed to kill Ardashir, who she says is no longer human, that Blight Miasma in the North Wuling Exclusion Zone is spiking because of Nefarith's meddling with the Very Large Rift, and that the pair are trying to open the Rift because of the Endmin. Zhuang sees a chance to strike first with the Nexus, and Arcane, though barely recovered, insists on leading the Yinglung Special Task Force herself. The team sets out for the bastion of Yinglung Pass.

On the way a voice only the Endmin can hear greets them. At the Pass, Summit hands command back to Arcane as Blightshades, enemies that look like lost Yinglungs, pour out of the Miasma. The Feranmut Proxy, Si, returns from tracing the Miasma's source. She treats the Endmin as an old acquaintance, scolds the Endmin for forgetting her and for calling her an Ink Spirit, dismisses Arcane's plan to fight through the Blightshades, and says the real priority is strengthening the Nexus with a ritual. She also hands over a gift: Ardashir, who gave himself up and is now bound in a prison she built inside the Scroll. Arcane explains that Blightshades are information fragments of Æther victims, once rare and short-lived, now attacking in numbers as if fleeing the Zone.

Questioned, Ardashir says they merely opened the Rift and do not truly understand the Æther, just as Terrans used Originium for ten thousand years without knowing its nature; he says he was born a Terran without Æther powers. He calls himself a past follower of the Endmin who survived by finding the Endmin before the End, says he and Nefarith serve the same Lady, and wants to make the Endmin lord of all to end conflict. Asked about the Foundation, he says the truth must be witnessed at the Rift. Perlica later explains that the Foundation was a Precursor organization seen during the First Aggeloi War and thought destroyed by the Endmin and the heroes of Terra, and alerts the Order of Steel Oath and M3.

Si's ritual, which she says an acquaintance taught HAS and which recalls the beacon fires of a city called Yumen, has the Endmin light altars and the three Balepyre Towers to focus the Feranmut power she left in the Pass. The augmented Nexus is handed over, and Si stays behind to keep the Miasma from Wuling while hiding her concern. Wuling's forces gather, with Mi Fu, Lifeng, Da Pan and many volunteer Tianshi and watchguards, and Tangtang and Qingwu tag along, Tangtang blaming the Rift for the feud with Wuling. In the Zone the first Sentry Base and Tianshi Pillar rise. Zhuang admits the weight of the day, Lifeng hopes to recover his parents' belongings, and Da Pan finds a cask of kohl at his late friend Old Sen's eatery and swears to finish the Rift.

At the Boundary, an old pillar left by Yinglung instructors, Arcane reveals she was the only child carried out of the depths ten years ago, passed from rescuer to rescuer, and that she has chosen this spot as her own resting place. At Tanjian Hall, the school where her generation grew up, her unhealed injuries show and Chen Qianyu and Summit make her rest. Pale Blightshades appear, among them their instructor Zhu, who seems to guide the team, and the howlerbeast Blitzcrash that Arcane raised. Chen confides that Arcane seems to care nothing for her own life. Zhu's last words remind both women why they joined, and Arcane wonders whether she has drifted from that purpose. At the ruined Xiranite Research Labs, Zhuang finds the Station's surviving data and the memorial to Project Xiranite, which carries the Endmin's name.

As the Xiranite Bridge toward the Rift is finished, tremors destroy it and Arcane falls into the gorge. The Endmin, whose Protorig had reacted to something, leaps after her and treats her wounds. Below lie the ruins of her childhood neighbourhood, where a pale Blightshade with a red ribbon turns out to be her younger self. It leads them past echoes of her parents debating a move to Hongshan, of a rescuer sheltering her, and of Zhu founding Tanjian Hall. At the source of the tremors stands a colossal sword thrumming with Æther, which the Endmin contains with the Nexus. When the Blightshades vanish as if the disaster replays, the Endmin uses Originium to bring them back and tells Arcane her rescuers entrusted her with hope, not despair. She finally says goodbye.

Data on the sword shows it was made by someone, of unknown material, and is almost a rift in itself; Perlica links it to the Exiles. Arcane admits the sword gave her grief a target, yet she now trusts the Endmin and a future without sacrifice. After the battle at the Rift, which is not shown, the Endmin announces that it is sealed; Si arrives in time to hold back the returning Miasma, and Wuling rejoices. Perlica reflects on an enemy from beyond the Rift and the Aurora moving north. M3 explains that Alleikhreos, a construct of the Foundation, has returned. Arcane plans to leave with the Yinglungs and perhaps teach. A badly wounded Nefarith reaches Ardashir's prison with a Protocol-Originium fragment, rejects his call for a sovereign, kills his body and promises to meet him on Talos-V. Si sees the Æther is harming the Endmin and prepares a treatment.
lore: This process names the threat behind the whole story so far. M3 says the Foundation are several individuals who created the Ankhors and Aggeloi, command the enemies of Terra and were once wardens of the Precursors; they believe Terran civilization must be enslaved. A century ago, in the First Aggeloi War, the Endmin banished them to the Ætherside. Alleikhreos, the enemy faced at the Rift, is their construct, and Nefarith says it clings to life in the Ætherside on plundered Protocol-Originium, so the crystal the Endmin used against the Exiles also kept them alive. The Æther-charged greatsword raises the question of whether the Wuling Science Station disaster was an accident at all. Possibly the Very Large Rift was a doorway the Exiles used, though the text leaves this open.

Talos-II is shown as a world settled from Terra: Ardashir speaks of ten thousand years of Originium Arts from Terra to Talos-II, and Arcane compares how Talosians see the Blight to how people of the Age of Terra regarded the Originium Catastrophes, as natural disasters rather than enemies. Perlica's mention of the heroes of Terra, the Order of Steel Oath and the Aurora above the Veil, and Arcane's list of Yinglung foes such as the Aurora of the North and the Shore Beyond, widen the map of Æther dangers beyond Wuling. Dijiang is called the largest Protocol-Originium on Talos-II, tying the Endmin's power to that material.

The Endmin's past deepens. Ardashir claims to be a former follower who survived the End by finding the Endmin, and speaks of dying Universes relying on the Endmin's arbitration; Si says that all of them knew the Endmin; the Endmin's name stands on Wuling's Xiranite memorial.
